overview: White plays the waiting move a3 in an open-game position, perhaps preparing b4 or Nc3 and Bb5 ideas, but losing time. Black can develop freely with ...Nf6, ...Nc6 or ...d5 and gets at least equality. It is a rare, offbeat tempo-loss, not a theoretical system.

white_ideas.idea: Prepare b4 or Ba2 ideas and play a Vienna or Italian structure with an extra a3
Transpose to an open game with Nf3 and Bc4
Take Black out of known theory

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...Nf6/...d5 and develop with tempo
Play ...Nc6 and ...Bc5 as in an Italian with an extra move
Equalise easily and use the spare tempo

typical_structures.structure: Open-game structures with e4/e5 and White having lost a tempo

character.notes: A waiting move; play is neither forcing nor passive.

soundness.notes: Sound but slightly inaccurate; gives Black a free tempo.

structure.notes: Centre undecided; likely transposes into Open Game structures.

approach.notes: Very rare among strong players; a pure surprise.

level.notes: Few concrete lines; no clear plans.

character.reason: A tempo-losing waiting move with no forcing play or special solidity.
